machine: Intel Core i9-10980XE; Studio window 1920x1080 kept off-screen; one rustc from another session was running
method: A copy of RH1_sphere_grid on C: with extra unshadowed point lights (range 10 m, on a grid over 40 m, so every ground pixel is lit by dozens to hundreds of them). Same build and scene; the only difference between runs is EUSTRESS_GPU_CLUSTERING. EUSTRESS_PROFILE=1; the phase profiler's reports after a 10 s settle are averaged, the first of each run left out. The engine's own count of PointLight instances was read over the bridge.

lights_303.reading: No frame-time difference outside the run-to-run spread (CPU 35.0 and 40.7 ms; GPU 40.0 and 38.6 ms): the scene is bound by the GPU's shading. CPU clustering adds about 2.3 ms of main-thread work a frame (PostUpdate 4.8 ms against 2.5 ms).

cpu_clustering.note: about 285 lights reach each ground pixel; the frame is the GPU's shading time

gpu_clustering.failure: The GPU device is lost about 3 s after start ('Caught DeviceLost error: Unknown Unexpected error variant (driver implementation is at fault)'), then bevy_pbr::cluster::gpu::prepare_clusters_for_gpu_clustering panics on its invalid buffer and Studio goes down (bevy_pbr-0.19.0 cluster/gpu.rs:1156).

lights_1503.reading: With Bevy's GPU clustering this scene takes Studio down, twice in two starts; with CPU clustering it opens and runs.

determinism: CPU clustering: two captures of a still scene are byte-identical (5 of 5 self-tests). GPU clustering: 5 of 5 differ, by 2 to 7 pixels of 8,294,400.
not_measured: a scene bound by the main thread, where the added CPU work would show in the frame time
